In plant taxonomy, commelinids (originally commelinoids [ 1 ] [ 2 ] ) is a clade of flowering plants within the monocots , distinguished by having cell walls containing ferulic acid . [ 3 ] [ 4 ] Well-known commelinids include palms and relatives (order Arecales ), dayflowers , spiderworts , kangaroo paws , and water hyacinth (order Commelinales ), grasses , bromeliads , pineapples , rushes , and sedges (order Poales ), ginger , cardamom , turmeric , galangal , bananas , plantains , and bird of paradise flower (order Zingiberales ).
